headline_en: A lesson in ideal foreign policy in a world that has lost its way!
Five Bangladeshis including a woman honoured for sending remittance from Italy
summary_en: The Bangladesh Embassy in Rome gave its 'Remittance Award' on 2 April 2024 to five expatriates (four individuals including one woman, and one business) as the top remitters from Italy for July 2022 to June 2023. The event also covered government services for expatriates, the Universal Pension Scheme and legal-channel remittance initiatives.

facts.statement: On 2 April 2024 at 4:30 pm the Bangladesh Embassy in Rome held a ceremony giving 'Remittance Award' crests to five expatriate Bangladeshis, including one woman, to encourage sending remittance through legal channels.

The Rome embassy's 2023 Remittance Award went to the highest remittance senders from Italy to Bangladesh in July 2022 to June 2023: individual (male) category Uddin Zia, Md. Mahfuzul Haque and Md. Omar Faruk; individual (female) category Mehenas Tabbasum; institution category Nibash Chakraborty, proprietor of Kaf PC Point.

The Rome embassy event included discussion of Bangladesh government services and activities for expatriates, the benefits of the Universal Pension Scheme (Sarbajanin Pension Scheme) and simplification of its registration process, and government initiatives for legal-channel remittance.
Ambassador to Italy Md. Monirul Islam told expatriates in Italy that the embassy is working sincerely to solve passport-related problems and to raise the quality of other services.

The Bangladesh Embassy in Rome introduced the 'Remittance Award' in 2019 to encourage legal-channel remitters; the award ceremony could not be held on International Migrants Day (18 December) for unavoidable reasons and was held on 2 April 2024 instead.

headline_en: BGB has protested the border killings: Foreign Minister
summary_en: Foreign Minister Hasan Mahmud told reporters on 28 March 2024 that BGB had protested and held border meetings over two Bangladeshis shot dead by India's BSF at the Lalmonirhat and Naogaon borders on 25 and 26 March. Asked about worker recruitment in Malaysia, he said the embassy had been told to hold talks to resolve the workers' crisis and that talks with Malaysia's foreign minister and labour ministry were planned. He also spoke about the hijacked ship's sailors and Dr Yunus.

facts.statement: Asked on 28 March 2024 about worker recruitment in Malaysia, Foreign Minister Hasan Mahmud said the Bangladesh embassy had been instructed to hold talks to resolve the workers' crisis, that Bangladesh had discussed it with the Malaysian ambassador in Dhaka, and that there was a plan to talk with Malaysia's foreign minister and labour ministry.
On the EU ban on importing Malaysian palm oil, Foreign Minister Hasan Mahmud said there are many places to sell palm oil and that Bangladeshi workers would not be inconvenienced by it.

Two Bangladeshis were killed by fire from India's Border Security Force (BSF): one at the Lalmonirhat border on 25 March 2024 and one at the Naogaon border on 26 March 2024. BGB protested and held border meetings.

According to the foreign minister's account of the BSF version, at Lalmonirhat some Bangladeshis cut the barbed-wire fence and crossed into India; when challenged they surrounded BSF members, BSF fired and two were injured, one returned to Bangladesh and the other was admitted to hospital on the Indian side and later died. He said the Naogaon incident on 26 March was similar, caused by crossing into India.
facts.source_in_article: Foreign Minister Hasan Mahmud citing BSF

facts.statement: Foreign Minister Hasan Mahmud said Bangladesh has long been discussing with India, including on his recent India visit, that non-lethal weapons be used at the border, and that such weapons are now used much more than before, so many people are injured by rubber bullets or pellets and return to Bangladesh.

On Bangladeshi sailors held hostage by Somali pirates, Foreign Minister Hasan Mahmud said the government was in contact to free the sailors, was making multi-pronged efforts to rescue the ship and sailors safely, had 'come a long way', and that there was no food shortage on the ship.

headline_en: Three sentenced to life imprisonment in human trafficking case in Jhenaidah
summary_en: On 20 March 2024 the Human Trafficking Offences Prevention Tribunal in Jhenaidah sentenced three absconding accused from Maheshpur to rigorous life imprisonment. They had taken away a 13-year-old girl in December 2011 on the promise of sewing-machine work; her mother filed a case in May 2012 alleging she had been trafficked inside or outside the country.

facts.statement: On 20 March 2024 at about 11 am, Judge Mizanur Rahman of the Human Trafficking Offences Prevention Tribunal (Manob Pachar Oporadh Domon Tribunal) in Jhenaidah sentenced Rowshanara Begum, Chhanowar Hossain and Bappi Hossain of Nalpatua village, Maheshpur upazila, to rigorous life imprisonment in a human trafficking case. All three are absconding; the sentence takes effect from the day of arrest or surrender.

According to the case summary, the three accused visited a family in Sonardari village, Jhenaidah Sadar, through a family acquaintance and repeatedly offered to arrange sewing-machine work for the family's 13-year-old daughter. On the morning of 28 December 2011 the girl's mother handed her over in front of some local people; the mother had contact with the girl for three months, then contact was cut and the accused stalled when asked to return her.

After the accused refused to return the girl on 13 May 2012, the mother filed a case under the human trafficking law at Jhenaidah Sadar police station on 31 May 2012 alleging the girl had been trafficked within the country or abroad. Police filed the charge sheet on 20 July 2012; the verdict came on 20 March 2024.

headline_en: Make a list of those conspiring against the country from abroad: Foreign Minister to expatriates
summary_en: At a reception by Bangladeshi expatriates in Abu Dhabi on 9 March 2024, Foreign Minister Hasan Mahmud asked expatriates to list people who conspire and spread propaganda against the country from abroad and urged them to remit through legal channels. Expatriates raised demands on Bangladeshi schools, an education quota, passports, remittance subsidy and Wage Earners' Bond problems.

facts.statement: At a reception by UAE-based Bangladeshis at an Abu Dhabi hotel on Saturday 9 March 2024 at about 9:30 pm local time, Foreign Minister Hasan Mahmud called on expatriates to make a list of those who conspire, spread propaganda and vilify the country from abroad, saying the government is determined to take appropriate action against them, and said expatriates should refrain from activities against law and order abroad.
Foreign Minister Hasan Mahmud urged expatriate Bangladeshis in the UAE to send remittance home through legal channels, saying it plays a big role in the economy.

Expatriates at the Abu Dhabi reception asked the foreign minister to intervene on: demands of the local Bangladeshi schools, an education quota in Bangladesh for expatriates' children, easier passport issuance and other services for expatriates in Bangladesh, recognition of remittance senders, a subsidy on sending remittance, and resolving complications with the Probashi Wage Earners' Bond.

headline_en: Young Bangladeshi volunteers shine at Asian Cup in Qatar
summary_en: Many Bangladeshi expatriates in Qatar are working as unpaid volunteers at the AFC Asian Cup 2023 starting 12 January 2024, as over a hundred did at the 2022 FIFA World Cup. Volunteers this time were recruited only from foreigners living in Qatar. The ambassador praised them and promised embassy help.

facts.statement: The AFC recruited about 6,000 volunteers for the AFC Asian Cup 2023 in Qatar (12 January to 10 February 2024); according to volunteer Satyaranjan Roy, this time volunteers were recruited only from foreigners living in Qatar and none were taken from outside Qatar.

More than a hundred Qatar-based Bangladeshi youths volunteered without pay at the 2022 FIFA World Cup and all later received certificates of honour and prizes from FIFA; many are again volunteering at the AFC Asian Cup in their free time after work. Shakil Ahmad of Sylhet, who works in the Qatar army, is one of them.

Labour and Employment Minister Ariful Haque Chowdhury told parliament that, in line with the government's election pledge, steps have been taken to form an 'Employment Exchange', which he said would make the employment system more transparent, merit-based, fair and decentralised.

headline_en: Export products must be diversified to capture the Malaysian market
summary_en: In an interview as Bangladesh and Malaysia began the first three-day round of free trade agreement (FTA) talks in Dhaka, Bangladesh-Malaysia Chamber president Md. Anwar Shahid said the FTA can be concluded by the December 2027 deadline set by the two heads of government. He said easing manpower export to Malaysia must be part of the FTA talks and that Bangladesh should train skilled people for technology and higher-value services.

facts.statement: Bangladesh and Malaysia have started negotiations on a free trade agreement (FTA); the first round, lasting three days, was under way at the Pan Pacific Sonargaon Hotel in Dhaka in late October 2026, and the two heads of government have set December 2027 as the deadline to complete the agreement.
facts.source_in_article: reporter; Md. Anwar Shahid, president, Bangladesh-Malaysia Chamber of Commerce and Industry

facts.statement: Md. Anwar Shahid, president of the Bangladesh-Malaysia Chamber of Commerce and Industry, said easing manpower export to Malaysia must be included in the FTA talks; Bangladeshis going abroad are still mainly in low-skill work, and raising their skills for technology and other high-value services would raise income.

Anwar Shahid said manpower export is usually thought of as construction or plantation workers, but there is scope in technology and skill-based work such as semiconductor design; if trained, even a few hundred such workers abroad could bring significant income, so training must match market demand.

Anwar Shahid said Bangladesh has started moving quickly on trade agreement talks with 10 to 12 countries because it will lose trade benefits after LDC graduation; Malaysia has FTAs with 14 countries including India and Pakistan; and four-five or even six-seven meetings may be needed for the Malaysia talks.

headline_en: Shahed's body handed over to family, to be buried at village home in Bogura
summary_en: The body of Bangladeshi worker Shahed Ahmmed, killed in a Houthi attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on 10 October 2026, arrived in Dhaka on Friday 23 October 2026 and was handed to his wife in the presence of the state minister for foreign affairs. Two Bangladeshis died in that attack, and the state minister said three Bangladeshis had been killed in missile attacks in Saudi Arabia in the past month, with only Shahed's body returned so far.

facts.statement: On 10 October 2026 Bangladeshi worker Shahed Ahmmed of Madla village, Shajahanpur upazila, Bogura, was killed in an attack by the armed group Houthis on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. Two Bangladeshis died in that attack; the other was Nasrullah Badarpuri of Nangalkot upazila, Cumilla.

Shahed Ahmmed worked as a plumber on the Jeddah project of a Saudi contracting firm and had a work permit (iqama); he was returning to his workplace in Jeddah via Riyadh after a one-month leave in Bangladesh and was at Riyadh airport when it was attacked.

Shahed Ahmmed's body reached Dhaka and was handed over to his wife Kohinur Akter at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport on the morning of Friday 23 October 2026, 13 days after his death, in the presence of State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam; the family left for Bogura in a hearse.

State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam said on 23 October 2026 that three Bangladeshis had been killed in missile attacks in Saudi Arabia in the past month; only Shahed's body had come home so far and efforts were under way to bring back the others quickly.

headline_en: Going abroad for higher study: what you must know before packing your bags
summary_en: A pre-departure checklist for students going abroad for the first time: documents to carry, airline and luggage rules, clothes, medicines and electronics, and arrangements for arrival. It quotes Shafiqul Islam Shimul, founder and CEO of BD Expert Education Consultancy.

facts.statement: Students leaving for study abroad should carry passport, visa, air ticket, the university offer letter and admission papers; if needed also academic certificates, transcripts, scholarship papers, proof of financial capacity and accommodation details, and should check in advance whether the destination country requires health-related or other documents.

Keep originals safe, make several sets of photocopies and digital copies, and keep important documents in hand luggage rather than checked luggage; check passport and visa validity, ticket date, flight time, and that the name on the ticket matches the passport.

For international flights the usual advice is to reach the airport at least three hours before departure, but the airline's instructions should be followed; find out beforehand whether the flight is direct or has a transit, whether a change of aircraft is needed and whether there is enough time for the next flight.

Luggage weight and size limits differ by airline, so check the baggage policy given with the ticket, what is allowed in hand luggage, the limit on liquids and which items are banned; carrying banned or restricted items can cause trouble at the airport.

Shafiqul Islam Shimul, founder and CEO of BD Expert Education Consultancy, said passport, necessary medicines and valuables should be in hand luggage, and that accommodation, transport and emergency contacts should be arranged before arriving abroad.
facts.source_in_article: Shafiqul Islam Shimul, BD Expert Education Consultancy

facts.statement: Regular medicines should be carried in their original packets; for prescription medicines carry the doctor's prescription and check the destination country's rules on carrying medicines. Choose clothes for the destination's weather and avoid overloading luggage.

Pack phone, laptop, chargers, cables and a power adapter and check that devices are compatible with the destination country's sockets and voltage; keep digital copies of important files on the phone or secure online storage.

Before travel, fix where you will stay, how you will get from the airport to accommodation and whom to contact in an emergency; save contacts of the university's international student support office, the housing authority and acquaintances; learn the local emergency number; and have phone internet and necessary cash or an internationally usable card ready.

headline_en: Why did the MP who said 'corpse of sin' make a U-turn
summary_en: An opinion column on the execution (beheading) of two Bangladeshi citizens in Saudi Arabia, which Bangladeshi authorities say they learned of only from media reports. It criticises the state minister for foreign affairs for calling it a 'lesson' and saying little can be done, a BNP MP for saying he did not want the 'corpse of sin' brought home (later withdrawn with an apology), and opposition parties' silence, and argues embassies must ensure lawyers, consular contact, appeals and clemency pleas.

facts.statement: Two Bangladeshi citizens were tried, sentenced to death and executed (an MP's post describes it as beheading) in Saudi Arabia; Bangladeshi authorities say they knew nothing beforehand and learned of it after media reports. Full details of the charges and trial had not been published as of 19 October 2026.

State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam said the execution of two Bangladeshis in Saudi Arabia 'is a big lesson for us' and that 'when something happens under their law, there is not much for us to do' (quoted from Prothom Alo online and Bangla Tribune, 17 October 2026).
facts.source_in_article: State Minister Shama Obaed Islam, as quoted by the columnist

facts.statement: On 18 October 2026 Bangladesh's Ministry of Foreign Affairs called in the Saudi ambassador and asked for detailed information about the executions; a ministry official described it as a meeting rather than a 'summons'.

The columnist argues that when a citizen is arrested abroad, embassies must work to ensure he gets a lawyer, understands the charges and can state his case; Bangladesh cannot change a foreign court's verdict but can help appoint a lawyer, maintain consular contact, and pursue appeal and a plea to commute the sentence.

The column says a Sri Lankan citizen was recently sentenced to death in Saudi Arabia in a blasphemy case; the Sri Lankan government took diplomatic and legal steps, a special lawyers' team worked with Saudi lawyers, and the Saudi Supreme Court later overturned the death sentence.

BNP MP Kamruzzaman Ratan said on a Star News talk show that he would never hope for 'this corpse of sin' to come to Bangladesh, referring to the bodies of the two executed Bangladeshis; he later withdrew the remark fully in a Facebook post and apologised to the families and to expatriates.
facts.source_in_article: columnist quoting the MP's talk-show remarks and Facebook post

facts.statement: As of the writing of the column, no formal reaction to the executions had been received from Jamaat-e-Islami or NCP.

headline_en: USD 2.5 billion in remittance came through BRAC Bank in first nine months of the year
summary_en: Remittance received through BRAC Bank passed USD 2.5 billion (250 crore) in the first nine months of 2026, beating its 2025 record of USD 2.2 billion; the bank targets over USD 3 billion by year-end. The article lists the bank's products for expatriates and their families.

facts.statement: Remittance coming through BRAC Bank exceeded USD 250 crore (2.5 billion) in the first nine months of 2026, surpassing its 2025 record of USD 220 crore; the bank has set a target of more than USD 300 crore by the end of 2026.
BRAC Bank offers expatriates and their families a Probashi Virtual Savings Account, Probashi Poribar Account, TARA Probashi Poribar Account and Offshore Banking Unit services.
Expatriates can open a BRAC Bank account from abroad through the bank's digital e-KYC platform, and use the 'Astha' app for fund transfer, bill payment and opening DPS and FDR.

BRAC Bank has built a network with exchange houses in the Middle East, South-East Asia, Europe, North America and Asia-Pacific corridors, with host-to-host integration and API connectivity with international partners, and delivers remittance through its branches, sub-branches and agent banking network including in rural areas.
BRAC Bank holds 'uthan boithok' (courtyard meetings) with remittance-receiving customers to raise awareness about sending remittance through legal channels and about banking services.

headline_en: Government gives Tk 1,000 crore to keep Janata Bank's UAE operations alive
summary_en: The government provided AED 30 crore (about USD 8.17 crore, roughly BDT 1,003 crore) in capital so state-owned Janata Bank's four UAE branches can keep operating after the UAE central bank ordered them wound up for failing to maintain paid-up capital. The branches serve Bangladeshi workers and expatriates with remittance, accounts and bond investment.

facts.statement: The Finance Division of the Ministry of Finance instructed Janata Bank to send USD 81,677,104 to the UAE by Wednesday 9 September 2026, a capital injection of AED 30 crore (USD 8.17 crore, about BDT 1,003 crore), so that Janata Bank's four UAE branches in Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Sharjah and Al Ain can continue services.

Under UAE central bank rules Janata Bank should hold paid-up capital of AED 40 crore in the UAE but had AED 10 crore, a shortfall of AED 30 crore. The UAE central bank wrote to the bank several times in 2026; its latest letter set a deadline and asked for an administrator to be appointed to wind up operations, told branches to stop opening new customer accounts or offering any new service, and restricted withdrawals from Janata Bank's account at the UAE central bank.

Bangladeshis in the UAE can send remittance through Janata Bank's four UAE branches (Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Sharjah, Al Ain) and open savings, current and term accounts; the branches also offer investment in the Wage Earners Development Bond and US Dollar Premium Bond, and open LCs, give commercial guarantees and commercial loans for Bangladesh-UAE trade.
Janata Bank has operated in the UAE since 1976; its services there are used by Bangladeshi workers and expatriate Bangladeshis.

headline_en: Family of banned Chhatra League leader Monirul, involved in attack on Badhon, lock house and leave village
summary_en: Monirul Hawlader (24) of Madaripur, an Italy-based leader of the banned Chhatra League, was reported involved in an attack on actress Azmeri Haque Badhon in Mestre near Venice on the night of 7 September 2026. After activists and intelligence personnel came to his village home on 8 September, his family locked the house and left. His stepbrother said Monirul went to Italy via Libya through a broker about a year and a half earlier for 28 lakh taka, and that the debt is still on his mother and brother.

facts.date: about early 2025 (a year and a half before September 2026)
facts.statement: Monirul Hawlader (24) of Khalanikandi, Dhurail union, Madaripur Sadar, travelled to Italy via Libya through a broker (dalal) about a year and a half before September 2026, paying 28 lakh taka, according to his stepbrother Obaidul Hawlader.

The 28 lakh taka paid for Monirul Hawlader's Libya-to-Italy journey left a debt that still rests on his mother and elder brother; he has not been able to build a house at the village home, where the family has two dilapidated tin-shed rooms.

After Monirul Hawlader was reported involved in an attack on and harassment of actress Azmeri Haque Badhon at a park in Mestre, Italy, on the night of Monday 7 September 2026, people including local Anti-Discrimination Student Movement and National Citizen Party activists and intelligence personnel came to his Madaripur home on 8 September; the family locked the house and fled.

Madaripur Additional Superintendent of Police (Crime and Sadar Circle) Fariha Rafiq said that since the incident happened abroad, action against Monirul would be taken under that country's law, and that police were alert so nobody could attack the family's home.

Monirul was organising secretary of the banned Chhatra League's Dhurail union unit and left Bangladesh after the mass uprising of 2024; the union parishad chairman said he has heard Monirul still does Chhatra League politics from abroad.

headline_en: Told his wife 'I got a promotion'; died in explosion in Russia before the month ended
summary_en: Zakir Hossain of Bhairab, Kishoreganj, was among 15 people killed in an explosion at the Amur Gas Chemical Complex in Russia in late August 2026. He had gone to Russia on 4 February 2025 at a cost of 7 lakh taka raised by selling land and borrowing, earned about BDT 60,000 a month, and about 1.5 lakh taka of debt remains. The family is waiting for his body; the UNO promised efforts to bring it back and is considering financial help.

facts.statement: An explosion at the Amur Gas Chemical Complex in Russia on a Tuesday (about 25 August 2026) killed 15 people, including Bangladeshi worker Zakir Hossain of Atkapara village, Kalikaprasad union, Bhairab upazila, Kishoreganj; his body was recovered on the following Thursday. A linked headline says one Bangladeshi worker was killed and another was missing.

Zakir Hossain was sent to Russia on 4 February 2025 at a cost of 7 lakh taka: 4 lakh from selling land, 2 lakh as a loan from an NGO, and the rest also borrowed. About 1.5 lakh taka of debt is still outstanding.

Zakir Hossain's job was at the Amur Gas Chemical Complex in Russia with a salary of about BDT 60,000 (in Bangladeshi currency); after his own costs he could not send much home and what he sent went to repaying loans. He had been promoted less than a month before his death and told his wife his pay would rise.

Bhairab Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) K M Mamunur Rashid said the administration will make every effort to bring Zakir Hossain's body home and is considering whether the poor family can be given financial assistance. The family learned of the death on Friday from his cousin Ali Hossain, who lived with him in Russia.

headline_en: Dollar price in open market Tk 126.50
summary_en: On Monday 24 August 2026 the Money Changers Association of Bangladesh (MCAB) announced an open-market dollar rate: buying at BDT 125.50 and selling at BDT 126.50, after the rate had recently risen to BDT 128 and Bangladesh Bank tightened supervision. MCAB's president said money changers deal only in cash foreign currency, mainly from returning passengers and migrant workers, and cannot bring in remittance directly.

facts.statement: From 24 August 2026 money exchanges in Bangladesh are to buy US dollars at BDT 125.50 and sell at BDT 126.50 (BDT 1 more), under a rate announced by the Money Changers Association of Bangladesh (MCAB); the open-market rate had recently risen to BDT 128 and Bangladesh Bank had stepped up supervision of money changers.

MCAB president M S Zaman said money changers only buy and sell cash foreign currency, do not transact electronic or virtual currency and cannot bring in remittance directly; cash foreign currency brought by returning passengers and migrant workers is the main source of their business.
MCAB communicates the dollar rate to all money changers in the country through the association's website.

MCAB's president blamed banks, not money changers, for manipulation in the dollar market and demanded clear instructions for money changers, more scope for legal dollar transactions and easier policy to shut the illegal market.

headline_en: Mamun, arrested at airport on allegation of involvement in extremism, remanded for 3 days
summary_en: Md. Mamun Hossain (26) of Munshiganj was detained at Dhaka airport's immigration at about 1:30 am on 20 July 2026 while, by his account, leaving for Qatar on a labour visa, and was remanded for three days on allegations of links to an extremist organisation. He said he is on bail in two anti-terrorism cases and no court barred him from travelling; the judge asked whether he had taken court permission to go abroad. The prosecution said he went to France via Portugal in 2020 and was sent back that year over alleged extremist activity.

facts.statement: Md. He told the court he was going to Qatar on a labour visa.

In court Mamun said two Anti-Terrorism Act cases against him are under trial but he is on bail in both and no court had prohibited him from going abroad; the Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate (Md. Jewel Rana) responded: 'You have misused the law. Did you take any permission from the court to go abroad?'

Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Md. Jewel Rana rejected bail and granted three days' remand for Mamun Hossain on 20 July 2026; the investigating officer, CTTC SI Md. Motiur Rahman Molla, had shown him arrested under section 54 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and sought seven days.

headline_en: Returned from abroad does not mean expatriate: the reality behind the label
summary_en: An opinion piece by the president of Bangladesh Press Club, Kuwait, objecting to news reports that label people caught at Bangladesh's airports with gold, mobile phones or other goods evading customs duty as 'expatriates' without verification. He asks media and customs officials to check length of stay abroad, visa type and residency before using the label.

facts.statement: Moin Uddin Sarkar Sumon, president of Bangladesh Press Club, Kuwait, writes that people detained at Bangladesh's airports for customs evasion with gold, mobile phones or other goods are often called 'expatriates' in news without verification, which harms the image of Bangladeshis working legally abroad.

The writer says before identifying a detained returnee as an expatriate, media, authorities and customs officials should verify how long the person stayed abroad, what type of visa they held (worker, business, student or tourist), whether their residency was valid, and whether they were a long-term expatriate at all.

key_quote_bn: বিদেশ থেকে এসেছেন বলেই কাউকে ‘প্রবাসী’ হিসেবে চিহ্নিত করা তথ্যের যথার্থতা নিশ্চিত করে না।

headline_en: Diplomacy of national interest and Bangladesh's new journey
summary_en: An opinion column by a migration professor at Universiti Brunei Darussalam arguing for multi-directional, interest-based diplomacy. It says Malaysia matters for Bangladesh's labour market, expatriate welfare and skill export, that the lives and income of lakhs of Bangladeshi workers depend on that relationship, and that government-to-government talks cover lowering recruitment costs, easing visas and protecting migrants.

facts.statement: Columnist Dr A K M Ahsan Ullah (professor of international, security and migration studies, Universiti Brunei Darussalam) writes that the lives, income, dignity and safety of lakhs of Bangladeshi workers depend on relations with Malaysia, so high-level talks with Malaysia are diplomacy tied to people's livelihoods, not a symbolic visit.
facts.source_in_article: columnist Dr A K M Ahsan Ullah

facts.statement: The columnist lists as part of government-to-government talks: whether recruitment costs in labour markets can be reduced, whether visas can be eased, whether migrants' protection can be ensured, and whether student and research exchange can be increased.
facts.source_in_article: columnist Dr A K M Ahsan Ullah

key_quote_bn: বাংলাদেশের লাখো শ্রমিকের জীবন, আয়, মর্যাদা ও নিরাপত্তা মালয়েশিয়ার সঙ্গে সম্পর্কের ওপর নির্ভরশীল।

headline_en: A new template of multi-directional diplomacy: significance of the Prime Minister's three visits
summary_en: An opinion piece by the Prime Minister's deputy press secretary on Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's June 2026 visits to Malaysia, the Summer Davos in Dalian and Beijing. In Putrajaya on 22 June he asked Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim to consider regularising Bangladeshis who had become irregular and renewing work permits, and requested recruitment of skilled workers; with Kazakhstan's prime minister he discussed sending skilled workers to Kazakhstan.

facts.statement: At a meeting at the Prime Minister's Office in Putrajaya on 22 June 2026 (10 am local time), Prime Minister Tarique Rahman asked Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim to consider regularising Bangladeshi nationals who had become irregular for various reasons and renewing their work permits, and requested the Malaysian government to recruit skilled workers from Bangladesh. The article reports the request, not a decision by Malaysia.
facts.source_in_article: Shahadat Swadhin, Deputy Press Secretary to the Prime Minister

facts.statement: The Bangladesh-Malaysia prime ministers' talks covered the free trade agreement (FTA), halal economy, semiconductors, higher education, vocational training, tourism, energy, defence, AI, digital economy, cyber security and modern technology; a joint statement of 33 points on 9 areas of cooperation was issued. The visit lasted 18 hours.
facts.source_in_article: Shahadat Swadhin, Deputy Press Secretary to the Prime Minister

facts.statement: On the sidelines of the World Economic Forum's 17th 'Summer Davos' in Dalian, China, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman held a bilateral meeting with Kazakhstan's Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov that discussed setting up permanent diplomatic missions in Dhaka and Astana and sending skilled workers from Bangladesh to Kazakhstan, along with energy, digital infrastructure and technology cooperation.
facts.source_in_article: Shahadat Swadhin, Deputy Press Secretary to the Prime Minister

facts.statement: In Beijing, Bangladesh and China signed 17 memoranda of understanding (13 at ministry level, 3 between BIDA and Chinese organisations, 1 between BNP and the Communist Party of China); representatives of at least 12 Chinese companies made investment proposals said to total more than USD 900 crore (about BDT 1 lakh 10 thousand crore).
facts.source_in_article: Shahadat Swadhin, Deputy Press Secretary to the Prime Minister

key_quote_bn: বিভিন্ন কারণে অনিয়মিত হয়ে যাওয়া বাংলাদেশি নাগরিকদের নিয়মিতকরণ এবং ওয়ার্ক পারমিট নবায়নের বিষয়টি মালয়েশিয়ার প্রধানমন্ত্রী আনোয়ার ইব্রাহিমকে বিবেচনায় নেওয়ার আহ্বান জানান।
